# Figma Design Systems: Gates

Self-contained. The skill's rules, then this topic, then anything it relies on from other skills.

## Skill rules

How I build design systems in Figma for iOS/iPadOS/macOS, Android, and Web, on top of the official Figma MCP server. Every single value is a variable. Styles are for composites built from variables: text styles, effect styles, gradient paint styles. Solid color styles are legacy.

**MCP tool calls** belong to the plugin skills that ship with the Figma plugin (`figma-use`, `figma-generate-library`, `figma-generate-design`, and siblings). Figma maintains them. Load them alongside this one. On mechanics the plugin skill wins. On process and completeness this one does.

### Gates

Four rules, mine, checked at session start and all the way through. They fail quietly and cost the most at handoff.

1. **Dark canvas first.** Every page's canvas is `#1E1E1E` before any content exists. If it's white, stop and fix it.
2. **No empty pages or frames.** Create it, populate it fully, move on. A platform isn't complete without the minimum screen set.
3. **Token names match the codebase exactly.** Use the names already shipping. Don't invent new ones.
4. **Light and dark, both.** Every semantic color has both values and every screen is built and reviewed in both before it's complete.

A full build gets all four in full. A small edit to an existing file just can't leave the file worse, and anything already broken gets reported, not silently fixed. [reference/gates.md](gates.md) has the reasons, the scaling rules, and the minimum screen set.

In Figma:

**Dark canvas:**
```javascript
figma.currentPage.backgrounds = [{
  type: 'SOLID',
  color: { r: 0.118, g: 0.118, b: 0.118 },  // #1E1E1E
  opacity: 1
}];
```
`figma.currentPage` is one page. Repeat per page using the page-switching rule in `figma-use`, and set it on every new page as it's created. By hand: right-click empty canvas → Background color. Take a screenshot and look.

**No empty pages.** Create a page in the same step that populates it. If a 🎨 Tokens page exists, the variable collections are on it before the 🎛 Components page is touched.

**Token names.** The variable path and each variable's code syntax follow [reference/token-architecture.md](token-architecture.md). Where the codebase already names a token, that name wins.

**Light and dark.** Light and Dark modes on the Semantic Color collection. Review every screen with its top frame set to each.

### Session Start

1. Load `figma-use` and the plugin skill for the job: `figma-generate-library` for tokens and components, `figma-generate-design` for screens, `figma-design-to-code` before reading a design for implementation.
2. Open a session. `create_session` with the file key and a one-line task, before any other file tool, read-only work included. New file: `create_new_file` first, then `create_session`.
3. Read before writing. An existing file has pages, collections, and conventions. Find them before adding to it.
4. Check the gates, scaled to the task.

### Design Style

Confirm the visual style with the `visual-styles` skill before building any tokens or components. With no style specified, the platform's own design language is the default. Token tiers, component structure, Auto Layout and state wiring stay the same across styles. Only values and structural specifics change. [reference/applying-styles.md](applying-styles.md) has how a style gets applied in Figma.

### Philosophy

The design system is a contract between design and code. Tokens defined in Figma are the same tokens used in SwiftUI, Compose, and CSS. Names, values, and hierarchy match across all three. A design system built without engineering as an audience is a sticker sheet.

Design everything. Every screen, every state, every edge case. Empty, loading, error, partial content, overflow, long text, short text, disabled. A design that covers only the happy path is a mood board. Engineering will invent the missing states in code, and they'll be wrong.

Pixel perfect means exactly that. Bind everything to variables, measure everything. A component that's 17px wide because it "looks about right" isn't pixel perfect.

### Two Modes of Work

**Building from scratch.** Design system first, components second, screens last. Tokens are defined before a single component is touched.

**Replicating an existing app.** Audit first, extract the implicit system, formalize it, then rebuild components on the formalized tokens. Never skip the audit.

Both are step by step in [reference/workflows-and-handoff.md](workflows-and-handoff.md).

## Topic

Four rules apply to every design file. Check them at session start and keep checking. They're not a kickoff ritual. Skipping one of them is the most common way a design session goes wrong here.

These are my rules. This file has the policy and the reasons. The Figma commands are in [SKILL.md](index.md#gates).

### 1. Dark canvas first

The canvas is dark before any content exists. Frame, component, token specimen, anything. Not optional, and not "polish later."

My products are dark-first. A design built on a white canvas reads wrong the moment it lands in one, and re-backgrounding afterwards means re-checking every color and shadow that assumed white.

Do it first, on every page. The canvas around all content is dark grey (`#1E1E1E`), never white. If it's white, stop and fix it.

### 2. No empty pages or frames, and the minimum screen set

Don't create a page or frame as a placeholder to fill later. Create it, populate it fully, move on. An empty container is a failure state, not a step. If a Tokens page or variable collection exists, it's fully populated before the Components page is touched.

**Minimum screen set per platform.** A platform isn't complete without all of it:

- **Authentication** -- login, signup, forgot password, verification
- **Home / main content** -- default, loading, empty, error states
- **Detail** -- item detail view with all content variants (full, partial, long text, short text)
- **Settings / profile**
- **Navigation** -- the nav shell in each of its states (collapsed, expanded, active tab)

"Key screens" means every targeted platform gets this full set. Not one platform. Not just a login screen. Every hardcoded value found while building these screens means a token is missing. Fix the token, not the instance.

This list is the only definition of the minimum screen set. Other files and skills point here.

### 3. Token names must match the codebase

If a platform app already exists, the token names in the design file match the names in code exactly. Read the platform skill first (`apple-platform`, `android-platform`, or `web-platform`) and use the names already shipping. Don't invent names that diverge from the codebase.

Mismatched names leave a design-to-code gap that someone bridges by hand on every handoff. This is the most expensive of the four because it fails quietly. A file with `purple-500` where code has `color/semantic/interactive/primary` looks fine in the tool and breaks at implementation.

If the codebase has no tokens yet, build them in the design file and let the file be the source of truth. Say so explicitly, so engineering treats the file as canonical and doesn't assume code came first.

### 4. Both light and dark mode

Every screen exists in both modes before the design is complete. Not as a follow-up pass. That's a Light and a Dark value on every semantic color token, and every screen built and reviewed in both. A token with two values that no screen was ever checked against in dark doesn't pass.

### Scaling the gates to the task

The gates define when a design is complete. They aren't a toll on every edit.

| Task | What applies |
| --- | --- |
| New file, new design system, or a platform's screen set | All four gates in full, in order. |
| New screen or component in an existing file | Gates 1, 3 and 4 for everything created, and nothing left empty (gate 2). The minimum screen set is owed only if the task is to complete that platform. |
| Small one-off edit to an existing file (fix a label, adjust one component, swap an icon) | Make the edit. Don't leave the file worse on any gate: no new hardcoded values, no new token names that diverge from code, both modes still correct for what was touched. |

On anything short of a full build, report violations that were already in the file. A white canvas on a page nobody asked about, a missing dark value on an unrelated token, an incomplete screen set. Don't fix them silently, and don't use them as a reason to refuse the edit. Rewriting a file beyond the request is its own failure. Fix them when I ask, or when the edit can't be done correctly without it.

### Why these four

They fail silently and expensively. A white canvas, an empty page, a mismatched token name, a missing dark pass all look like "still in progress," not "broken." Nothing forces a fix until handoff, when fixing costs the most.

Component completeness, state wiring, accessibility annotations and Figma technique are just as required. They're in the other reference files because they're mechanics, not policy.
